clue.text: Abel's murderer? It could be him

definitions.meaning: Cain, who killed Abel, was the third human after Adam and Eve, so the third individual in the Bible story
pronouns such as it and him belong to the grammatical category used for someone spoken about

explanation.walkthrough: Cain followed Adam and Eve, making him humanity's third individual; grammatically, 'it' and 'him' are pronouns of that same category.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar's term for the speaker-excluded, listener-excluded pronoun class covers 'it' and 'him'; Cain was the Bible's third human.

clue.text: Announcement of van's arrival by jingly tune in street play

definitions.text: Announcement of van's arrival by jingly tune in street
definitions.meaning: an ice-cream van plays a jingle to announce its seller is arriving, read humorously as a proclamation

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain ice-cream vans tour streets playing a jingle; the title of O'Neill's play reads as that jingle's message.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene O'Neill wrote this stage drama, set in a New York saloon, first produced in 1946.

clue.text: Times spinning bits of news?

indicators.note: spinning sets the letters of the word Times whirling into a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper's stories go round and round, like spin doctors at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning' scrambles TIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: News items are individual reports or pieces of information in a paper or bulletin.

clue.text: Give girl brief call

parts.note: Di is the brief, shortened form of the girl's name Diana
to call is to shout

explanation.surface: Pass a young woman a short telephone message.
explanation.definitionFit: To dish out something is a phrasal verb meaning to hand it out or distribute it.

clue.text: Female tagger-on with philosopher, one making an effort

parts.note: the suffix -ess is tagged on to make a female form, as in lioness
A. J. Ayer was a British philosopher

explanation.surface: A woman who follows a philosopher around is trying hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay is to attempt, so one who essays is someone trying or attempting something.

clue.text: Inexperienced male put into position, inadequate person lacking substance

indicators.note: put into says the following pieces are placed inside the other word
inadequate tells us the word for position falls short of its final letter

parts.note: a stand is a position, as in taking a stand
raw means inexperienced, as in a raw recruit

explanation.surface: A green young man placed in a post is an inadequate, insubstantial figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inadequate' looks like part of the definition but trims the position word by its last letter; 'put into' then signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurehead or weak stand-in with no real substance is a common idiomatic sense, also a misrepresented argument.

clue.text: Gambling system one I try? Not at all, silly

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters of the phrase are jumbled into nonsense and rearranged

parts.words: one I try? Not at all

explanation.surface: Someone vows never to try the gambling scheme, calling it silly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' scrambles all fifteen letters of ONE I TRY NOT AT ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's state-run lottery, launched in 1994, is a prize draw on which people bet money on numbers.

clue.text: Looking hard, having lost a thread

indicators.note: having lost means a letter of the word for looking hard is dropped

parts.note: staring is looking hard

explanation.surface: Someone peers closely after dropping a cotton thread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost' removes the A from STARING.
explanation.definitionFit: Thread and twine are near synonyms: thin cord or yarn.

clue.text: We hear fish'll cook

indicators.note: we hear tells us the answer sounds like the spoken phrase

parts.note: a cod is a fish, and cod'll (cod will) is pronounced like the answer

explanation.surface: Rumour has it the fish will cook.
explanation.definitionFit: To coddle is to cook eggs gently in water just below boiling.

clue.text: The reverse of fat, the man's held to be a hero in Athens

indicators.note: held means one piece is kept inside the other
the reverse of means the word for fat is read backwards

parts.note: suet is hard animal fat
the man's is short for he's, he is

explanation.surface: A skinny Athenian man is regarded as a hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The reverse of fat' reads like 'thin' but means the fat word spelt backwards (TEUS); 'held' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary king of Athens slew the Minotaur, a celebrated Greek mythological hero.

clue.text: Way to avoid repeated note when having to in musical piece

indicators.note: to avoid indicates a letter is left out of the word for way

parts.note: a street is a way or road
E is a musical note, and the street word has two of them in a row, one dropped
to taken as it stands

explanation.surface: A musician seeks a way to dodge playing a note twice in a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeated note' points to the doubled E in the way word; 'to avoid' drops just one of the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: In a fugue, the final passage where entries overlap closely is called by this Italian term.

clue.text: Study icon having moved away from general society

indicators.note: having moved says the letters of the two words are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A revered student figure has withdrawn from public life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having moved' scrambles STUDY ICON.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone held under arrest or in prison is kept apart from the public at large.

clue.text: Tried to win, sounding disagweeable

indicators.note: sounding says the answer is pronounced like a word

parts.note: the misspelling mimics a speaker who says W for R, so rude becomes wude

explanation.surface: A suitor's wooing comes across as rude, lisped childishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disagweeable' shows a speech defect turning R into W: rude said that way is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To woo is to court someone, seeking their affection or hand in marriage.

clue.text: Electronic publication about cricket?

indicators.note: about here means turned around, the pieces read backwards

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail
a mag is a magazine, a publication

explanation.surface: An online magazine covering cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: E plus MAG make EMAG, which 'about' turns around. Cricket is a bat-and-ball sport popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket is one example of a sport, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Work at greyhound stadium to divert from the main point

definitions.meaning: in greyhound racing a mechanical lure is set running to begin the chase

definitions.text: to divert from the main point
definitions.meaning: the idiom means to raise a distracting side issue

explanation.walkthrough: Greyhounds chase an artificial lure round the track; the idiom originally comes from hunting, flushing an animal into the open.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatically, raising an irrelevant topic that sends a discussion off course.

clue.text: Girl I had upset, keeping quiet over dumping process

indicators.note: keeping means the outer letters hold the others inside
upset in a down clue turns the pieces upside down, read in reverse

parts.note: a lass is a girl
I'd is the short form of I had
P is piano, quiet in music
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A girl says she's upset at having quietly been dumped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses the girl and 'I had' together, giving DISSAL; 'keeping' holds the quiet and over letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting rid of waste or unwanted things is the act of throwing them away.

clue.text: Pieces can get mixed up left in that school box?

indicators.note: in says the letter for left goes inside the anagrammed letters
get mixed up says the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bits of stuff jumbled inside a schoolchild's box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get mixed up' rearranges PIECES CAN into PENCICASE, and 'in' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil carries pens and rulers to class in this small container.

clue.text: Answer phone in truck

definitions.meaning: to lift the receiver and take a call
a small open-backed lorry, chiefly American usage

explanation.definitionFit: A light open lorry is so called; lifting a receiver is the phrasal verb.

clue.text: Musical arrangement leader ignored — bad upset for composer

indicators.note: leader ignored means the first letter of the word for a musical arrangement is dropped

parts.note: a score is the written arrangement of a piece of music

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill feeling

explanation.surface: A band whose bandleader was ignored is badly upset over a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader ignored' cuts SCORE to CORE; 'upset' turns ILL into LLI.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcangelo Corelli was an Italian Baroque violinist who wrote concerti grossi.

clue.text: Pasquale's work environment

definitions.meaning: Pasquale is this puzzle's compiler, and a compiler's job is composing crosswords
a scene or surroundings in which something happens

explanation.walkthrough: Pasquale is the pseudonym of this puzzle's compiler; composing crosswords is called this.
explanation.definitionFit: Surroundings or backdrop, as the scene of a story, is the second sense.

clue.text: Criticise possible achievement of East-West partnership

definitions.meaning: in bridge, East and West play as partners, and winning every trick, or all but one, is a coup

explanation.walkthrough: Bridge is played by two partnerships named by compass points; winning twelve or thirteen tricks earns a big bonus.
explanation.definitionFit: To pan harshly is one sense; a contract for all or nearly all tricks in bridge is the other.

clue.text: Many inches around theologian's waist

indicators.note: around means the outer word goes around the other piece

parts.note: a mile contains a great many inches
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: A well-fed theologian's waistline runs to a great many inches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many inches' is a playful definition of a distance unit, not a number; 'around' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The waist is the midsection of the body, informally called by this word.

clue.text: Horse's rump given whip around third part of course

indicators.note: around means the word for whip encloses the selected letter

parts.note: a crop is a riding whip

indicators.note: third part of picks the third letter of the word course

explanation.surface: A jockey whips a horse's hindquarters on the third leg of the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'third part of' takes U, the third letter of COURSE; 'around' puts CROP round it.
explanation.definitionFit: The hindquarters of a horse, above the hind legs, are called by this term.

clue.text: Hesitation about pamphlet before editor's disowned

indicators.note: before places the pamphlet word ahead of the editor's abbreviation
about means the word for hesitation is turned round

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation
a tract is a pamphlet
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An editor hesitates over a pamphlet before taking it back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ER into RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract a statement is to withdraw it, taking back what one said.

clue.text: Presumably having lots of plants wonky?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, it says like Kew, the botanical gardens in London with a vast plant collection

explanation.walkthrough: Kew Gardens is London's royal botanic garden; something as Kew would have lots of plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Crooked or at an angle, not straight, is what wonky means.

clue.text: Nuts fixed to secure centre of wheel — then I left behind tool

indicators.note: to secure means the rearranged letters hold the central letter inside
fixed here means repaired or reworked, so the letters are rearranged
centre of picks the middle letter of the word wheel

explanation.surface: A mechanic tightens wheel nuts with a tool, then leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' rearranges NUTS into UTNS; 'to secure' holds E, the middle of WHEEL, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Any implement, especially a kitchen one, is called by this word.

clue.text: One knew about lines — something for pupil at school once?

definitions.text: something for pupil at school once?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: about means the letters of knew are moved about into a new order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: A pupil who knew about writing lines as punishment at school long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges KNEW into NKWE.
explanation.definitionFit: Old school desks held a small pot of ink for dipping pens, now a thing of the past.

clue.text: Like employers waywardly ruling

definitions.meaning: employers are holdings companies; waywardly says the word break is shifted

explanation.walkthrough: Move the space one letter: 'holdings way', the manner of companies that employ people, becomes the idiom for ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in control and wield influence over others is the idiom's sense.
